questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language — it is the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is the correct file extension for an HTML file?
questions.explanation: HTML files use the .html (or .htm) extension and are opened by web browsers.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which tag is the root element of every HTML page?
questions.explanation: The <html> element wraps the entire page and is the root of every HTML document.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: ____DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head></head>
  <body></body>
</html>
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> declares the document type and tells the browser this is an HTML5 document.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What goes inside the <head> tag?
options: Meta information, title, and links to CSS/JS
questions.answer: Meta information, title, and links to CSS/JS
questions.explanation: The <head> contains metadata like the page title, charset, and links to stylesheets — nothing visible on the page itself.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: <____>My Page Title</title>
questions.explanation: The <title> tag sets the text shown in the browser tab.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between the <head> and <body> sections of HTML?
options: They are identical — both show content
<head> holds page metadata (not displayed); <body> holds visible content
<body> holds page metadata; <head> holds visible content
<head> is for images; <body> is for text
questions.answer: <head> holds page metadata (not displayed); <body> holds visible content
questions.explanation: The <head> is for behind-the-scenes information (title, stylesheets, scripts). The <body> is what users actually see in the browser.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is an HTML tag?
options: A keyword surrounded by angle brackets like
questions.answer: A keyword surrounded by angle brackets like
questions.explanation: HTML tags are keywords enclosed in < > brackets that tell the browser how to format content.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE:

Hello World____p>
questions.explanation: Most HTML elements need a closing tag written as </tagname> to mark where the element ends.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which tag creates the largest heading in HTML?
questions.explanation: Headings go from <h1> (largest/most important) to <h6> (smallest). <h1> should be used once per page for the main title.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which HTML element creates a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The <a> (anchor) element creates a clickable hyperlink. The destination URL goes in the href attribute.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: Visit Google
questions.explanation: The href attribute specifies the URL that the anchor link points to.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between <div> and <span> in HTML?
options: They are the same element with different names
<div> is a block-level container; <span> is an inline container
<span> is a block-level container; <div> is inline
<div> is for images; <span> is for text
questions.answer: <div> is a block-level container; <span> is an inline container
questions.explanation: <div> takes up the full width (block), useful for layout sections. <span> wraps inline content without breaking the line flow.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which HTML element is used to create an interactive form?
questions.explanation: The <form> element is the container for all interactive controls like text fields, buttons, and checkboxes.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: <input ____ ="text" placeholder="Enter name">
questions.explanation: The type attribute on <input> controls what kind of input is shown (text, password, email, checkbox, etc.).

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which input type creates a submit button?
questions.explanation: type="submit" creates a button that submits the form data to the server.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does the <label> element do in a form?
options: Provides a clickable text description for an input field
questions.answer: Provides a clickable text description for an input field
questions.explanation: <label> improves accessibility by giving a text description to a form control. Clicking the label focuses the linked input.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: <input type="____" name="agree"> I agree
questions.explanation: type="checkbox" creates a toggleable checkbox input.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between GET and POST methods in a form?
options: GET sends data in the URL; POST sends it in the request body
POST sends data in the URL; GET sends it in the body
GET is for images; POST is for text
questions.answer: GET sends data in the URL; POST sends it in the request body
questions.explanation: GET appends form data to the URL (visible, bookmarkable). POST sends it hidden in the HTTP body — better for sensitive data.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What are semantic HTML elements?
options: Tags that only style the page
Tags that clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and developer
questions.answer: Tags that clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and developer
questions.explanation: Semantic tags like <header>, <nav>, <article> describe the role of the content, improving accessibility and SEO.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: <____> Home About
questions.explanation: <nav> is a semantic element that wraps the main navigation links of a page.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which semantic element represents a self-contained piece of content?
questions.explanation: <article> represents standalone content that could be distributed independently, like a blog post or news story.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What is the purpose of the alt attribute on an tag?
options: Provides alternative text if the image fails to load
questions.answer: Provides alternative text if the image fails to load
questions.explanation: The alt attribute describes the image for screen readers and displays as fallback text when the image cannot be loaded.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE:
questions.explanation: The src attribute specifies the path to the image file that should be displayed.

questions.prompt: RECALL: Why should you use semantic HTML instead of only <div> and <span>?
options: Semantic HTML improves accessibility, SEO, and code readability
questions.answer: Semantic HTML improves accessibility, SEO, and code readability
questions.explanation: Semantic tags help screen readers understand page structure, help search engines index content properly, and make code easier for developers to read.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It controls how HTML elements look — colors, fonts, layout, and more.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which HTML tag is used to link an external CSS file?
questions.explanation: The <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> tag inside <head> connects an external CSS file to the HTML page.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What is the correct CSS syntax to change text color to red?
questions.explanation: CSS uses property: value; syntax. The color property sets text color.
CSS rules use curly braces { } to wrap declarations. The selector (p) is followed by the opening brace.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which CSS selector targets an element with id="header"?
questions.explanation: The # prefix selects an element by its id attribute. IDs are unique per page.
The . (dot) prefix selects elements by their class name. Multiple elements can share the same class.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between class selectors (.) and id selectors (#) in CSS?
options: # is for multiple elements; . is for a single unique element
. selects multiple elements sharing a class; # selects a single unique element by id
. selects by tag name; # selects by attribute
questions.answer: . selects multiple elements sharing a class; # selects a single unique element by id
questions.explanation: Classes can be reused on many elements; IDs must be unique on a page. Use classes for repeating styles, IDs for one-off elements.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which CSS property changes the font size of text?
questions.explanation: font-size sets the size of text, e.g. font-size: 16px; or font-size: 1rem;
The color property sets the foreground (text) color of an element.

questions.prompt: SELECT: How do you make text bold using CSS?
questions.explanation: font-weight controls how thick/heavy the text appears. Values include bold, normal, or numeric weights like 700.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which CSS property sets the background color of an element?
questions.explanation: background-color sets the color behind an element's content, e.g. background-color: #1a1a2e;
font-family sets the typeface. You list fallback fonts separated by commas.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between px, em, and rem units in CSS?
options: px is relative to parent; em is absolute; rem is relative to viewport
px is an absolute pixel size; em is relative to parent font-size; rem is relative to root font-size
rem is absolute; em and px are both relative
questions.answer: px is an absolute pixel size; em is relative to parent font-size; rem is relative to root font-size
questions.explanation: px gives a fixed size. em scales relative to the parent element's font size. rem always scales relative to the root <html> font size — making rem more predictable.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is the CSS Box Model?
options: A concept that treats every element as a rectangular box with content, padding, border, and margin
questions.answer: A concept that treats every element as a rectangular box with content, padding, border, and margin
questions.explanation: Every HTML element is a box. The box model defines how its total size is calculated: content + padding + border + margin.
padding adds space inside the element, between the content and the border.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What is the difference between padding and margin in CSS?
options: Padding is space outside the element; margin is space inside
Padding is space inside the element (between content and border); margin is space outside the element
questions.answer: Padding is space inside the element (between content and border); margin is space outside the element
questions.explanation: padding creates breathing room inside the box. margin creates space outside the box, separating it from other elements.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which CSS property adds a visible line around an element?
questions.explanation: border draws a line around the element's edge. Example: border: 2px solid #333;
box-sizing: border-box makes width/height include padding and border, preventing unexpected layout overflow.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What does box-sizing: border-box do?
options: Adds a border to every element
Makes the element's total size include padding and border within the declared width/height
questions.answer: Makes the element's total size include padding and border within the declared width/height
questions.explanation: By default (content-box), width excludes padding and border. With border-box, padding and border are included — so width: 200px means 200px total.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is CSS Flexbox?
options: A one-dimensional layout model for arranging items in a row or column
questions.answer: A one-dimensional layout model for arranging items in a row or column
questions.explanation: Flexbox makes it easy to align and distribute space among items in a container, either in a row or column.
display: flex turns an element into a flex container, enabling flexbox layout for its children.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which CSS property centers flex items horizontally?
questions.explanation: justify-content controls alignment along the main axis (horizontal in a row). center places items in the middle.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does align-items: center do in a flex container?
options: Centers items vertically along the cross axis
Makes all items the same width
questions.answer: Centers items vertically along the cross axis
questions.explanation: align-items controls alignment on the cross axis (perpendicular to main axis). center aligns items vertically when flex-direction is row.
flex-direction sets whether items are placed in a row (default) or column.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items in Flexbox?
options: justify-content aligns on the main axis; align-items aligns on the cross axis
align-items aligns on the main axis; justify-content aligns on the cross axis
justify-content is for columns; align-items is for rows
questions.answer: justify-content aligns on the main axis; align-items aligns on the cross axis
questions.explanation: In a row flex container: justify-content is horizontal, align-items is vertical. They flip when flex-direction is column.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is JavaScript primarily used for?
questions.explanation: JavaScript adds interactivity to web pages — responding to clicks, updating content dynamically, and communicating with servers.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What extension do JavaScript files use?
questions.explanation: JavaScript files use the .js extension. They are linked to HTML pages using a <script> tag.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: console.____("Hello, World!");
questions.explanation: console.log() prints output to the browser's developer console — the standard way to debug JavaScript.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword declares a variable that can be reassigned in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: let declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned. const is for values that won't change. var is the older, less-preferred keyword.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: ____ name = "Aditya";
questions.explanation: const declares a constant — a value that won't be reassigned. Prefer const over let unless you need to change the value.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between let and const in JavaScript?
options: let is for strings; const is for numbers
let allows reassignment; const does not allow reassignment after initialization
const allows reassignment; let does not
questions.answer: let allows reassignment; const does not allow reassignment after initialization
questions.explanation: Use const for values you don't intend to change (most variables). Use let when you need to update the value later (e.g. a counter).

questions.prompt: RECALL: Where does JavaScript run — in the browser, server, or both?
options: In the browser (client-side) and also on servers via Node.js
questions.answer: In the browser (client-side) and also on servers via Node.js
questions.explanation: JavaScript was originally browser-only, but Node.js brought it to the server. Today it is the only language that runs natively on both client and server.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a JavaScript string?
questions.explanation: Strings are text values wrapped in quotes (single, double, or backtick). 42 is a number, true is a boolean.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: const age = 21;
console.log(____ age ____);
questions.explanation: Template literals use backticks and ${} to embed variables directly inside strings.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does typeof 42 return in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: JavaScript has one numeric type called number for both integers and decimals. typeof returns the type as a string.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which value represents 'nothing intentionally' in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: null means an intentional absence of a value (you set it deliberately). undefined means a variable exists but hasn't been assigned a value yet.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: const items = [1, 2, 3];
console.log(items.____);
questions.explanation: The .length property returns the number of items in an array.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
options: == checks type only; === checks value only
== checks value with type coercion; === checks value and type strictly
=== is for strings only; == is for numbers
questions.answer: == checks value with type coercion; === checks value and type strictly
questions.explanation: == converts types before comparing (5 == "5" is true). === requires same type and value (5 === "5" is false). Always prefer === to avoid bugs.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is a function in JavaScript?
options: A reusable block of code that runs when called
questions.answer: A reusable block of code that runs when called
questions.explanation: Functions let you define logic once and reuse it anywhere. They can accept inputs (parameters) and return outputs.
The function keyword declares a named function in JavaScript.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What is an arrow function in JavaScript?
options: A function that only runs once
A compact function syntax using => instead of the function keyword
questions.answer: A compact function syntax using => instead of the function keyword
questions.explanation: Arrow functions (const add = (a, b) => a + b;) are a shorter syntax introduced in ES6. They also don't have their own 'this'.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: const square = (n) ____ n * n;
questions.explanation: => is the arrow syntax for arrow functions. (n) => n * n is equivalent to function(n) { return n * n; }

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does a function return if there is no return statement?
questions.explanation: If a function has no return statement (or just return; with no value), it returns undefined.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between a function declaration and a function expression?
options: Declarations are hoisted and available before their code line; expressions are not hoisted
Expressions are hoisted; declarations are not
questions.answer: Declarations are hoisted and available before their code line; expressions are not hoisted
questions.explanation: function greet() {} is hoisted — you can call it before it appears in code. const greet = function() {} is an expression and cannot be called before its line.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is the DOM?
options: Document Object Model — JavaScript's representation of the HTML page
questions.answer: Document Object Model — JavaScript's representation of the HTML page
questions.explanation: The DOM is a tree-like representation of the HTML document. JavaScript uses it to read and modify page content dynamically.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: const btn = document.____("#submit");
questions.explanation: document.querySelector() returns the first element matching a CSS selector string.

questions.prompt: SELECT: How do you change the text content of a DOM element?
questions.explanation: textContent sets or gets the text inside an element, safely without parsing HTML. Use innerHTML only when you need to insert actual HTML tags.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What method attaches an event listener to a DOM element?
questions.explanation: addEventListener(eventType, handler) registers a function to run when the specified event (like 'click') occurs on the element.
The 'click' event fires when the user clicks on an element.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between innerHTML and textContent?
options: innerHTML is faster; textContent is slower
textContent is only for inputs; innerHTML is for all elements
innerHTML parses and renders HTML tags; textContent treats everything as plain text
questions.answer: innerHTML parses and renders HTML tags; textContent treats everything as plain text
questions.explanation: innerHTML can insert actual HTML (e.g. bold makes text bold). textContent inserts raw text — safer against XSS injection attacks.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a valid C source file extension?
questions.explanation: C source files have the .c extension. The compiler compiles these into executable programs.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does the C compiler do with your source code?
options: Runs it directly line by line
questions.explanation: A C compiler translates your human-readable source code into machine code that the CPU can execute.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which header do you need to use printf() in C?
questions.explanation: stdio.h declares standard input/output functions like printf and scanf.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Every C program must have exactly one function named:
questions.explanation: main() is the entry point the operating system calls to run your program.
The function signature int main() defines the program's entry point.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: printf("Hi")____
questions.explanation: Every C statement ends with a semicolon.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the purpose of return 0; at the end of main() in C?
options: It tells the OS the program finished successfully
questions.answer: It tells the OS the program finished successfully
questions.explanation: Returning 0 from main() signals to the operating system that the program ran without errors.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a valid variable name in C?
questions.explanation: Variable names must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits, and underscores.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which type holds a single character in C?
questions.explanation: char stores a single byte, typically one character.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does this declare? float price = 9.99;
questions.explanation: float declares a decimal number variable, here initialized to 9.99.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: ____ age = 25;
questions.explanation: int is the C keyword for a whole-number variable.
The + operator adds two integers together.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between int and float in C?
options: int is for text, float is for numbers
int is for whole numbers, float is for decimals
float is for whole numbers, int is for decimals
questions.answer: int is for whole numbers, float is for decimals
questions.explanation: int stores integers (e.g. 5, -3), while float stores decimal (floating-point) numbers (e.g. 3.14).

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which symbol is used to open a code block in C?
questions.explanation: Curly braces { } open and close code blocks in C, like after an if statement.
C uses curly braces { } to open a block after an if condition.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which operator checks equality (not assignment) in C?
questions.explanation: == compares two values; = assigns a value.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does != mean in C?
questions.explanation: != is the 'not equal' comparison operator.
i++ increments i by 1 after each loop iteration.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What happens if you write = instead of == inside an if condition in C?
options: It assigns a value instead of comparing — a common bug
questions.answer: It assigns a value instead of comparing — a common bug
questions.explanation: = is assignment, == is comparison. Using = in an if() condition assigns the value and may always be true or false — a tricky bug.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: How many parts does a C for loop header have?
questions.explanation: for (init; condition; update) — three parts separated by semicolons: initialization, condition, and update.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which loop is guaranteed to run its body at least once?
questions.explanation: do { ... } while(condition); checks the condition after running the body.
while(condition) repeats the block as long as the condition is true.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What keyword immediately exits a loop in C?
questions.explanation: break immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch.
break stops the loop as soon as i equals 5.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between break and continue in a loop?
options: continue exits the loop; break skips to the next iteration
break exits the loop entirely; continue skips to the next iteration
break is for while loops, continue is for for loops
questions.answer: break exits the loop entirely; continue skips to the next iteration
questions.explanation: break stops the loop completely; continue jumps to the top of the loop to begin the next iteration.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What does C++ use instead of printf() to print output?
questions.explanation: C++ uses std::cout (from <iostream>) as its standard way to output text.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which header provides std::cout in C++?
questions.explanation: <iostream> declares the standard input/output stream objects.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: std::cout ____ "Hello, World!";
questions.explanation: The << (insertion) operator sends data into the output stream.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'using namespace std;' let you do?
options: Define a new namespace called std
Drop the std:: prefix before names like cout
questions.answer: Drop the std:: prefix before names like cout
questions.explanation: It brings everything in the std namespace into scope, so you can write cout instead of std::cout.
Curly braces open the function body, just like in C.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What does std::endl do when used with std::cout?
options: It inserts a newline and flushes the output stream
It declares the end of a namespace
questions.answer: It inserts a newline and flushes the output stream
questions.explanation: std::endl outputs a newline character '\n' and flushes the buffer, ensuring output appears immediately.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these creates an unchangeable value in C++?
questions.explanation: const marks a variable as unmodifiable after initialization.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword declares a constant in C++?
questions.explanation: const marks a variable as unmodifiable after initialization.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: int x = 10;
int& ref = ____;
questions.explanation: int& ref = x; makes ref an alias that refers directly to x.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does the & symbol mean when placed after a type, e.g. int&?
questions.explanation: In C++, & after a type declares a reference variable (an alias to another variable).

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: std::string name = ____Ada Lovelace";
questions.explanation: C++ string literals are wrapped in double quotes.

questions.prompt: RECALL: If you modify a reference variable, what happens to the original?
options: The original is also modified, because they share the same memory
questions.answer: The original is also modified, because they share the same memory
questions.explanation: A reference is an alias — it points to the same memory location, so changes to the reference change the original.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is a function in C++?
options: A reusable block of code that performs a task
A way to store multiple values
questions.answer: A reusable block of code that performs a task
questions.explanation: Functions let you group code under a name so you can call it multiple times without repeating yourself.
return sends the computed value back to the caller.

questions.prompt: SELECT: In 'int add(int a, int b)', what does the first 'int' specify?
options: The return type of the function
questions.answer: The return type of the function
questions.explanation: The type before the function name declares what type of value it returns.

questions.prompt: SELECT: A function declared with return type 'void' means:
questions.explanation: void indicates the function performs an action but returns no value.
A function definition's closing brace needs no trailing semicolon (unlike a declaration).

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between a function declaration and a function definition?
options: A declaration provides the full function body; a definition only names it
A declaration tells the compiler the function exists and its signature; a definition provides the actual body
Declarations are for classes; definitions are for functions
questions.answer: A declaration tells the compiler the function exists and its signature; a definition provides the actual body
questions.explanation: A declaration (prototype) tells the compiler what the function looks like. A definition provides the full implementation.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What is a class in C++?
options: A loop that runs a fixed number of times
A built-in data type like int
questions.explanation: A class defines the structure (attributes) and behavior (methods) that objects created from it will have.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword defines a new class in C++?
questions.explanation: class Name { ... }; defines a new class blueprint.
d.bark() calls the bark method on the object d.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'public:' control inside a class?
options: Which members are accessible from outside the class
questions.answer: Which members are accessible from outside the class
questions.explanation: Access specifiers like public/private control visibility of members outside the class.

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: Dog ____ = Dog();
questions.explanation: This creates an object named myDog of type Dog.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between public and private members in a class?
options: public members can only be accessed inside the class; private ones from anywhere
public members are accessible from outside the class; private ones can only be accessed inside the class
public members are faster; private ones are slower
questions.answer: public members are accessible from outside the class; private ones can only be accessed inside the class
questions.explanation: Encapsulation: public members form the interface of the class, while private members hide internal details.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a Python source file?
questions.explanation: Python source files have the .py extension.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Python is best described as:
questions.explanation: Python is interpreted (run line by line) and dynamically typed (types are inferred at runtime).

questions.prompt: COMPLETE: ____("Hello, World!")
questions.explanation: print() outputs text to the console in Python.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which symbol starts a comment in Python?
questions.explanation: Everything after # on a line is treated as a comment.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Python uses ____ to define blocks of code instead of curly braces.
questions.explanation: Consistent indentation (spaces) defines code blocks in Python.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: name = ____World"
print(name)
questions.explanation: This string starts with a double quote, so it must also end with one.

questions.prompt: RECALL: Why doesn't Python need semicolons at the end of lines?
options: Each new line is treated as a new statement by default
Python uses brackets to end statements
questions.answer: Each new line is treated as a new statement by default
questions.explanation: In Python, a newline ends a statement, so semicolons are unnecessary (though valid if you want multiple statements on one line).

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: Which of these is a valid Python variable assignment?
questions.explanation: Python doesn't require a type keyword — just write the variable name, =, and the value.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Do you need to declare a variable's type in Python?
questions.explanation: Python is dynamically typed — you just assign a value and Python infers the type.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: age = 25
name = "Sam"
print(name, ____, age)
questions.explanation: String literals in a print() call must be quoted.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What type is the value produced by 3 / 2 in Python 3?
questions.explanation: The / operator always performs true division and returns a float in Python 3.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: items = ____
items.append("apple")
questions.explanation: Square brackets [] create an empty list in Python.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the result of type(3.14) in Python?
questions.explanation: 3.14 is a decimal literal, so Python infers its type as float. type() returns the class of the value.

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY: What character ends an if statement header in Python?
questions.explanation: In Python, if statements end with a colon, followed by indented code on the next line.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: if score >= 60____
    print("Pass")
else:
    print("Fail")
questions.explanation: Python uses a colon to start a block, followed by an indented line.

questions.prompt: SELECT: Which keyword checks another condition after an initial 'if' fails?
questions.explanation: Python's keyword for 'else if' is elif.

questions.prompt: SELECT: What does 'and' do between two conditions in Python?
options: True if either condition is true
True only if both conditions are true
questions.answer: True only if both conditions are true
questions.explanation: The 'and' logical operator requires both sides to be true.

questions.prompt:
COMPLETE: for i in ____(5):
    print(i)
questions.explanation: range(5) generates numbers 0 through 4 for the loop to iterate over.

questions.prompt: RECALL: What is the difference between 'and', 'or', and 'not' in Python?
options: and = at least one true; or = both true; not = adds
They all mean the same thing
and = addition; or = subtraction; not = multiplication
